land.text: the page says only that the Cochise tradition "appears to be ancestral" to the Mogollon and Hohokam; no year or land is given

successors.note: Hohokam is the other named descendant; neither has a dossier.

correction.text: "in the present-day Southwestern United States"; Willcox Playa, Cochise County, Arizona; Ventana Cave and "other locations in Arizona and western New Mexico"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The Cochise tradition lasted nearly five millennia, from circa 5000 until circa 200 BC." Arizona and south-west New Mexico (1,202 land cells, about 304,000 km2) stand for "the present-day Southwestern United States"; the page names no frontier and no area.

region.text: "in the present-day Southwestern United States"; Willcox Playa, Cochise County, Arizona; Ventana Cave and "other locations in Arizona and western New Mexico"

ledger.note: 5000 BCE: the Cochise tradition begins in the Southwest. "The Cochise tradition lasted nearly five millennia, from circa 5000 until circa 200 BC." Year and the Arizona and western New Mexico places (Willcox Playa, Ventana Cave) are the page's; the region drawn is the dossier's.

3500 BCE: the Chiricahua phase. "The phase has been dated to between about 3500 and 1500 BC, but its beginnings may be much earlier"; occupations in Ventana Cave and "other locations in Arizona and western New Mexico". The earlier Sulphur Spring phase has no dates on the page.
1500 BCE: the San Pedro phase. "Provisional radiocarbon dates have shown San Pedro flourishing from about 1500 to 200 BC."

region.text: "in the present-day Southwestern United States"; Willcox Playa, Cochise County, Arizona; Ventana Cave and "other locations in Arizona and western New Mexico"

ledger.note: 200 BCE: the Cochise tradition ends. "from circa 5000 until circa 200 BC"; the Mogollon and Hohokam, for which it "appears to be ancestral", are not dated on the page, so the land passes to nobody and the two are kept as successors in the identity.

certainty.note: A tradition known from sites, not frontiers.

sources.title: Cochise culture
sources.note: Cochise tradition c. 5000 to c. 200 BC; Chiricahua phase about 3500-1500 BC; San Pedro 1500-200 BC; Arizona and western New Mexico; ancestral to Mogollon and Hohokam.

sources.title: Archaic period (North America)
sources.note: Archaic 8000-1000 BC; Middle Archaic mounds from 3500 BC; Old Copper complex 4000-1000 BC; Oshara 5500 BC-500 AD; Cochise.

notes: Cochise culture, southern Arizona and western New Mexico. The Cochise page has no infobox and gives no dates for the Sulphur Spring phase. The Archaic-period page lists "2500 BC: The Cochise tradition become skilled farmers of the American Southwest", not used for the extent. Mogollon and Hohokam (named successors) have no dossier here; the Oshara tradition is the northern neighbour (the New Mexico border is the dossier's).
